title: Metric-slice-driven canary gated by quality signatures for version-lock rollouts
creator: Ayesha Khan
description: Goal: Provide a reproducible, metric-slice-driven canary workflow that validates new model revisions behind a version-lock (revision lock) before promotion. This workflow must prioritize user-visible quality signals (semantic correctness, hallucination rate, rerank recall) alongside system SLOs (p50/p99 latency, error rate, token cost). The canary will run as a gated experiment where small cohorts receive the candidate revision while the rest remain on the locked revision. Gate decisions are driven by pre-published quality signatures and per-slice checks rather than a single global metric.
background: We onboard many open and internal model revisions and publish performance profiles per revision. Current rollouts rely on coarse global metrics and manual checks; incidents and regressions have been caught late. Product needs: safe promotion path for version-locked routes used by enterprise customers, automated rollback criteria, and observability that ties regressions back to specific metric slices (e.g., long-context prompts, code generation, brevity prompts).
acceptance_criteria: Canary config UI lets PM/Eng choose candidate revision, cohort size (0.1% -> 10%), and metric slices to evaluate
Automated quality signatures published per revision and visible in Console (precision/recall proxies, hallucination estimate, toxicity filter hit rate)
Gate engine evaluates configured slices every 5 minutes and returns PASS/WARN/FAIL with rationale

Rollback triggers: FAIL on any critical slice (semantic regression >4% absolute), or system SLO breach (p99 latency increase >25% or error rate >1%). These triggers cause an automated traffic rollback and an incident ticket creation
Experiment dashboard shows per-slice diff between candidate and baseline with confidence intervals and sample prompts for investigation
Playbook documented with manual override, post-mortem template, and owner assignment
updates: 2026-03-01: Scoped initiative with Research, Serving, Console, and Observability teams. Drafted hypothesis and initial gating rules.
2026-03-03: Design review — added explicit per-slice sample exposure so PMs can review failing examples before rollback.
2026-03-05: Engineering prototype for metric ingestion completed (depends on ENG-2987 for KV cache telemetry extension).
2026-03-07: UX mockups for canary config in Console linked in docs; requested accessibility tweaks from design.
2026-03-09: Rules engine SPI (server-side) implemented; currently running end-to-end tests against synthetic workloads.
2026-03-10: Discovered gap — hallucination proxy metric needs better calibration on long-context tests. Added mitigations to acceptance criteria.
decisions: Use cohort-based holdout (randomized tenant buckets) rather than user-sampling to respect consistent user experience and CSAT tracking.
Define quality signatures as a fixed set of automated evaluations (truth-labeled prompt families + heuristics) published with each revision profile.
Primary gating signal will be per-slice delta with bootstrap confidence intervals; global aggregates are advisory only.
Automated rollback is enabled for high-severity slices but requires human approval for non-critical WARN states.
A/B experiments (parallel traffic) are supported for deeper analysis, but default onboarding flow uses incremental canary to minimize blast-radius.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: False positives on quality signals due to small sample sizes. Mitigation: enforce minimum sample thresholds per slice before applying FAIL and use bootstrap CIs.
Risk: Metric instrumentation gaps (e.g., hallucination proxy). Mitigation: temporary soft-fail gates and add labeling for auto-generated examples to track calibration.
Risk: Enterprise routes with strict SLAs see contention. Mitigation: allow per-route disable and read-only promotion for locked routes until explicit approval.
Risk: Complexity of UI leads to misconfiguration. Mitigation: provide safe defaults, presets (low/medium/high safety), and a validation check on save.
implementation_notes: Engineers will extend rollout-service to accept a 'slices' config list (name, query, threshold, severity). Observability will forward per-slice time-series and example buckets to Grafana/Trace. Console will add a compact canary summary card for locked revisions with quick rollback and a link to sample prompts. Post-deployment, Research will run a diversified eval suite (1000 prompts per slice) to validate the published quality signature before enabling automated PASS/FAIL behavior.
